title: Combined Thymosin β4 and Thymosin α1 in Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A 12-Month Prospective Open-Label Case Series
content: Background/Objectives: Primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) has few effective treatments, and the only approved therapy modestly slows disability progression. PPMS is driven by compartmentalized inflammation and failed remyelination; thymosin β4 (Tβ4) promotes remyelination in experimental demyelination, and thymosin α1 (Tα1) restores regulatory immune responses that are deficient in MS. We explored the tolerability and functional course of combined Tβ4 and Tα1 in PPMS. Methods: In this prospective, single-arm, open-label case series, eight wheelchair-dependent adults with PPMS (age 52.0 ± 5.5 years) who were off disease-modifying therapy received subcutaneous Tβ4 2.5 mg and Tα1 2.5 mg weekly for 12 months, without rehabilitation. The NuRaX Ambulation Grade (1–4; study-specific, unvalidated) and upper- (UEMS) and lower-extremity motor scores (LEMS) were recorded at baseline and every 3 months and summarized descriptively. Results: All participants completed dosing. Ambulation improved from grade 3 to grade 2 (walking with an elbow crutch) in 5/8 participants by month 3 and 8/8 by month 9, and was maintained at month 12. From baseline to month 12, mean LEMS increased from 34.5 ± 1.4 to 43.6 ± 1.1 (+9.1; 95% CI 8.0–10.3). The four participants with baseline upper-limb deficits improved, mostly within 3 months; the other four were at the UEMS maximum throughout. Transient nausea after the first two doses occurred in 3/8 participants. Conclusions: Combined Tβ4 and Tα1 was well tolerated and accompanied by improved ambulation and lower-limb strength. These uncontrolled observations give an early indication that the combination may benefit people with PPMS, but require confirmation in a randomized controlled trial.
